builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Prior Predictive Matching for Bayesian LoRA
summary: This technique replaces manual or validation-based selection of the prior scale in Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with a closed-form estimator derived from prior-predictive matching before fine-tuning. It costs a one-time analytical computation and eliminates the need for validation data or repeated hyperparameter sweeps, but it relies on a second-order expansion of the network that may be inaccurate for highly nonlinear tasks and assumes that the estimated prior precision generalizes across adaptation ranks, which can fail if the task or model violates these scaling assumptions.
rationale: The method enables practitioners to set Bayesian LoRA priors analytically without validation data or costly tuning, delivering validated improvements in predictive NLL and calibration on constrained infrastructure.
technique: Prior predictive matching for Bayesian LoRA

claims.statement: This technique replaces manual or validation-based selection of the prior scale in Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with a closed-form estimator derived from prior-predictive matching before fine-tuning. It costs a one-time analytical computation and eliminates the need for validation data or repeated hyperparameter sweeps, but it relies on a second-order expansion of the network that may be inaccurate for highly nonlinear tasks and assumes that the estimated prior precision generalizes across adaptation ranks, which can fail if the task or model violates these scaling assumptions.

On RoBERTa-large, the method improves predictive negative log-likelihood (NLL) and calibration over both MAP and marginal-likelihood selection, while achieving competitive out-of-distribution detection.
